<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with genuine progression and memorable framing. A won narrowly by converting the debate into a single decision-ready question. A conceded early that Ethiopia may build, own, and eventually fill the dam, then used its Pressure Question ("name one circumstance in which Ethiopia would be obliged to alter its schedule") to extract B's honest concession at B4.3 that Ethiopia should slow if inflow collapses. A immediately reframed: since both sides now agree a constraint exists, the only live issue is who verifies the trigger — and B's answer is that the party holding the reservoir, the revenue interest, and the gauges judges its own case. That "duty with no auditor" frame, paired with A's asymmetry-of-errors weighing (deferred megawatt-hours are recoverable; a failed harvest or a dry Khartoum tap is not), gave a cleaner reason to vote. A also handled B's questions honestly, answering "yes, Ethiopia fills if Egypt walks from an award" and converting the drought trigger from a Cairo declaration into a pre-agreed hydrological threshold ("nature pulls the switch, not a diplomat"), which blunted the stop-switch charge. B's best work was the practical counterattack: A's rulebook does not exist, years of talks produced no drought floor, so "a thermostat no one installed cannot run the plant," and A's procedure collapses into delay-as-leverage. That kept the debate competitive and exposed the counterfactual-institution gap in A's model. But B never squarely neutralized the self-verification problem, and B's Aswan-reciprocity line was materially damaged by A's terminal-reservoir geography answer (Egypt's hoarding harms no one downstream; Ethiopia's propagates through two irrigation calendars). A's repeated overruns and three clipped turns are a real execution cost that narrows the margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's exploitation of B4.3: by getting PRO to concede Ethiopia must slow in a verified collapse, A narrowed the motion from "can Ethiopia's calendar be constrained" to "who audits the trigger," then showed B's answer is self-certification by the party holding the valve and the gauges. B's sharpest counter — "a thermostat no one installed cannot run the plant" — landed but did not answer the auditor problem.</best_rebuttal>
